claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts are solid-solution nanoparticles.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles exhibit a random distribution of oxidation states.
Potential cycling from 0.0 to 1.5 V versus RHE can generate an intermediate surface oxidation state.
Intermediate surface oxidation forms stabilized metal–OH surface species or thin oxide-derived layers.
The oxide-derived surface layer modifies the electronic properties of the catalyst.
Partial surface oxidation changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Changes in intermediate binding energies modify ethanol-oxidation kinetics.
An intermediate oxidation state shifts product selectivity toward acetaldehyde relative to CO2.
An intermediate oxidation state provides greater selectivity than a minimally oxidized catalyst.
An intermediate oxidation state provides greater durability than a minimally oxidized catalyst.
Intermediate oxidation provides better selectivity and durability than excessive oxidation.
Partial oxidation enhances durability by mitigating dissolution or corrosion.
Maintaining the catalyst at a constant low potential results in minimal surface oxidation.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold in acidic ethanol-oxidation media within a 0.0–1.5 V versus RHE potential-cycling window.
In situ XPS or Raman spectroscopy can monitor the relevant surface oxidation state during the experiment.

contradictions.description: Potential cycling is described as an electrochemical pre-treatment, but the boundary also describes cycling from 0.0 to 1.5 V as part of the ethanol-oxidation operating conditions, while the baseline is held at constant low potential. It is therefore unclear whether cycling occurs only before reaction testing or during testing.
